messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER: cont-batch perf cliff on prod-us-west2 - high tail latency and 5xx spike (>5% in 3m). Alert: https://alerts.internal/ALERT12345. Paging oncall.

oncall-sre: Acknowledged, grabbing telemetry now.

alice-eng: Seeing kvcache eviction rate spike ~10x on pool cb-pool-17. Queue backlog rising fast.

carol-obs: Dash links: https://dashboards.internal/r/cont-batch/17 - queue length went from ~20 -> ~1200 in <5m, p99 latency up to ~2.8s. Microbatch size collapsed then burst to 64 in retries.

bob-ml: Matches a KV cache blowup pattern — possibly a prefix invalidation storm or coalescer regression when concurrency high.

oncall-sre: Can we throttle ingress at the edge? Short of that, we can flip continuous_batching.enabled=false for that pool and fall back to microbatching. Fastest rollback.

dave-ps: Customer impact: CS flagged timeouts for AtlasInc (us-west2). SLA at risk. @erica-cs can you notify? :confused:

erica-cs: Pinged AtlasInc with a brief note, shared we have an active mitigation plan; asked for any traffic pattern changes on their side.

alice-eng: Proposed emergency hotfix: for cb-pool-17 -> set "continuous_batching.enabled": false, set "max_microbatch_size": 8, and add jitter to batch window (flip from fixed 4ms to [8,16]ms). Quick canary then roll.

bob-ml: +1. Canary on 10% of nodes (cb-canary-03, cb-canary-07). Watch KV-hit-rate and eviction metrics.

carol-obs: I'll spin up a canary dashboard and watch eviction-rate, kv-hit-rate, queue-length, p50/p90/p99. Preparing alerts to notify if regressions persist.

oncall-sre: Executing patch on canary: 
```
curl -XPOST https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/pools/cb-pool-17/config -d '{"continuous_batching.enabled":false,"max_microbatch_size":8,"batch_window_ms_min":8,"batch_window_ms_max":16}'
```

alice-eng: Patch applied to 10% and rolling.

carol-obs: Canary metrics: eviction-rate ↓ 78%, queue length → ~40, p99 latency 2.8s -> 650ms. KV-hit-rate recovered. Early signal good. :thumbsup:

oncall-sre: Scaling patch to 100% of pool now (rolling restart of batch workers, zero-downtime where possible).

erica-cs: Update sent to AtlasInc: hotfix deployed to their region, latency improving. They acknowledged, asking for ETA for permanent fix.

dave-ps: Note: smaller microbatches increase cost ~+10-15% for the pool. We'll need an optimization plan postmortem.

bob-ml: Root cause hypothesis: prefetch coalescer regression under extreme concurrency created duplicate prefix writes and forced hot eviction churn. Need trace replay and reproducible test.

alice-eng: Log excerpt from worker during spike:
```
[2024-11-12T17:35:04Z] kvcache: evict key shard=17 size=2048 reason=collision
[2024-11-12T17:35:04Z] batch: queued=1023 microbatch_size=64 caller=ingest
[2024-11-12T17:35:05Z] kvcache: evict key shard=17 size=4096 reason=dup_write
```

carol-obs: Metrics stabilized after full rollout. Setting a 1h hold window to watch for recrudescence.

oncall-sre: Handoff notes for next oncall at 18:00 UTC: 1) mitigation applied (continuous_batching disabled on cb-pool-17), 2) monitor eviction-rate, queue-length, p99 latency, 3) revert only after formal kernel/coalescer fix + canary. Links: canary dashboard, deploy logs, runbook.

erica-cs: Customer comms: AtlasInc notified, follow-up scheduled for postmortem.

dave-ps: Owners for postmortem: alice-eng (tech lead), carol-obs (telemetry), bob-ml (prefetch/model), dave-ps (prod owner). Action: reproduce in staging with high concurrency harness, add tighter e2e tests for batching jitter.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: cont-batch perf cliff on prod-us-west2. Duration: 00:11:26. Pager cleared.
